question: A parking garage had 102 cars in the morning. In the morning, 67 cars left for work. Later that morning, 25 more cars pulled in for a conference. In the afternoon, 58 cars left after the conference ended. That evening, 1 more car left for a late errand. How many cars were in the garage by the end of the evening?

A single charity's coin collection started the month with 117 dollars. The total was split evenly among 3 collection boxes, and this story follows just one box. A matching sponsor then multiplied that box's total by 7. A large withdrawal for event costs then cost the box 103 dollars. A late donation added 13 more dollars. Finally, a year-end match multiplied the box's total by 5. How much money was in that one box in the end?

A single beehive started spring with 54 worker bees. A cold snap cost the colony 8 bees. A warm spell then added 41 more bees. A strong nectar season left the hive with 9 times as many bees. A swarm split then cost the hive 741 bees. Finally, 3 more bees returned from a scouting trip, around the time a neighboring hive was said to hold about a dozen queen cells, unrelated to this count. How many bees were in the hive in the end?

A single food pantry shelf started the morning with 204 cans of soup. By midmorning, the cans were split evenly among 3 shelves, and this story follows just one shelf, whose cans were then split evenly again among 4 volunteers, following just one volunteer's share. In the afternoon, a matching donation left that share with 6 times as many cans, and 20 more cans were added from a grocery donation. That evening, 97 cans were given out to families, around the time a nearby shelf held about 50 boxes of pasta, unrelated to this count. Finally, a matching year-end drive multiplied the remaining cans by 7. How many cans did that one volunteer have by the end of the evening?

A single school fundraiser jar started the morning with 33 dollars. In the morning, 35 more dollars were added from early donors. By midday, a matching sponsor left the jar with 4 times as much money. In the afternoon, a second matching sponsor multiplied the jar by 9. That evening, a final matching gift multiplied the jar by 3, around the time a nearby jar collected about 60 dollars in loose change, unrelated to this jar. How much money was in the jar by the end of the evening?

Two collectors, Petra and Igor, keep coin jars, but this story follows only Petra's jar, which started at 185 coins, more than Igor's jar held. She spent 133 coins on a rare find. A trade then doubled her remaining coins. Her jar was then split evenly among 4 smaller pouches, and this story follows just one pouch. That pouch gained 3 more coins from a friend, then lost 3 coins to a vending machine. How many coins were in that one pouch in the end?

A single food bank shelf started the morning with 208 cans. In the morning, 164 cans were given out to families. Later that morning, 29 more cans arrived from a donation. In the afternoon, 47 more cans came from a school drive. That evening, a matching year-end donation multiplied the shelf's cans by 3. How many cans were on that shelf by the end of the evening?

Two vineyard owners, Selin and Gustavo, track grape crates, but this story follows only Selin's crates, which started at 148, more than Gustavo's vineyard had. She picked 77 more crates that morning, then 38 more, and 64 more later, after a harvest that took about 180 minutes, exactly 3 hours. A wholesale buyer's matching offer then left her with 6 times as many crates. Finally, a second matching offer left her with 2 times as many crates. How many crates did Selin have in the end?

A single movie theater started the evening with 220 seats reserved. A group of 5 canceled their reservation early. Then 62 more reservations were canceled after a schedule change. A further 19 seats were canceled due to a weather warning, around the time a second theater across town sold 300 tickets that night, unrelated to this count. Finally, 85 more reservations were canceled when a competing event was announced. How many reserved seats remained for this theater's showing?

A single farm's egg count started the morning with 103 eggs collected. By midmorning, a bumper lay left the coop with 6 times as many eggs. In the afternoon, the eggs were split evenly among 3 delivery crates, and this story follows just one crate. Later that afternoon, a matching order multiplied that crate's eggs by 7. That evening, 13 more eggs were added from a late collection. Finally, a holiday order multiplied the crate's eggs by 8. How many eggs were in that one crate by the end of the evening?

Two collectors, Wilhelm and Ayana, keep stamp albums, but this story follows only Wilhelm's album, which started at 158 stamps, more than Ayana's album held. He traded away 103 stamps at a swap meet. He then gave 31 more stamps to a fellow collector. A misplaced page cost him 7 more stamps, and a torn page cost 1 more, during a meet that lasted about 120 minutes, right around 2 hours. Finally, a matching gift doubled his remaining stamps. How many stamps were in Wilhelm's album in the end?

Two shop owners, Bianca and Levi, track their candle stock, but this story follows only Bianca's stock, which started at 47 candles, fewer than Levi's stock. A wholesale order left her with 9 times as many candles. A crafting session added 24 more candles. A festival contract then multiplied her stock by 7. A large order used up 86 candles, around the time a rival shop priced candles at 14 dollars each, unrelated to Bianca's count. Finally, 68 more candles arrived from a supplier. How many candles did Bianca have in the end?

Two runners, Delphine and Hugo, log training minutes, but this story follows only Delphine's log, which started at 59 minutes, fewer than Hugo's log showed. She logged 21 more minutes that morning, and 69 more that afternoon. A matching relay event then multiplied her logged total by 7. She then logged 37 more minutes from an evening run. A data error erased 874 minutes from her log, around the time her coach mentioned running about a dozen laps that day, unrelated to this count. Finally, 49 more minutes were added back after the error was fixed. How many minutes did Delphine's log show in the end?

A single grain elevator started the day with 135 bushels of wheat. A local co-op delivery left the elevator with 9 times as much wheat. A regional contract then multiplied that amount by 5. A rail shipment of 1875 bushels was sent out to a mill, after a loading process that took about 60 minutes, exactly 1 hour. A final harvest bonus multiplied the remaining wheat by 5 once more. Finally, 30 more bushels arrived from a late delivery. How many bushels of wheat were left in the elevator?

A single toy warehouse started the morning with 240 dolls in stock. By midmorning, a holiday order left the warehouse with 4 times as many dolls. In the afternoon, 238 dolls were sent to a damaged-goods return. Later that afternoon, a regional contract multiplied that count by 5, and a second contract multiplied it by 6, after a negotiation that took about 120 minutes, right around 2 hours. That evening, 3935 dolls were shipped out to stores, around the time a rival warehouse reported holding 700 dolls, unrelated to this count. Finally, a citywide order multiplied the remaining dolls by 4. How many dolls were in the warehouse by the end of the evening?

Two collectors, Farrah and Julian, count vinyl records, but this story follows only Farrah's collection, which started at 88 records, fewer than Julian's shelf held. She bought 66 more records at a flea market. A friend gave her 28 more, and an estate sale added 43 more. A dealer's matching offer then multiplied her collection by 5. A separate record store nearby stocked about a dozen rare imports, unrelated to Farrah's count. How many records did Farrah end up with?

A single grain silo started the harvest with 90 tons of barley. A delivery added 68 more tons that week. A bumper crop then doubled the silo's barley. A shipment removed 16 tons for a mill order, after a loading run that took about 60 minutes, exactly 1 hour. A second shipment removed 232 more tons. Finally, 18 more tons arrived from a late delivery. How many tons of barley were in the silo in the end?

A single museum archive started the year with 121 artifacts catalogued. A major donation left the archive with 7 times as many artifacts. A university partnership added 19 more artifacts. A loan to a partner museum then removed 626 artifacts. A local dig then added 46 more artifacts, and a second dig added 44 more. Finally, 23 more artifacts arrived from a private collector, around the time a curator mentioned displaying a dozen new photographs, unrelated to this count. How many artifacts were in the archive in the end?

Two friends, Marisol and Deng, keep separate coin jars, but this story follows only Marisol's jar, which started at 13 dollars, less than Deng's jar held. A birthday gift added 59 more dollars. A matching gift then doubled her jar. The money was then split evenly among 6 smaller envelopes, and this story follows just one envelope. Finally, 9 dollars were spent on a gift from that envelope. How much money was in that one envelope in the end?

A single toy warehouse started the morning with 116 dolls in stock. By midmorning, a holiday order left the warehouse with 6 times as many dolls. In the afternoon, a regional contract multiplied that count by 9. Later that afternoon, 17 more dolls arrived from a returned batch. That evening, a citywide order multiplied the dolls by 9 once more, after a shipment that took about 240 minutes, exactly 4 hours. Finally, 20 more dolls arrived from a late delivery, and 25118 dolls were shipped out to stores. How many dolls were left in the warehouse?

A single farm's egg count started the morning with 94 eggs collected. In the morning, 25 eggs were sold at the roadside stand. By midday, a bumper lay left the coop with 7 times as many eggs. In the afternoon, a regional order multiplied that count by 6. That evening, a holiday order multiplied the eggs by 6 once more. How many eggs did the farm have by the end of the evening?

Two shop owners, Ines and Baptiste, track candle stock, but this story follows only Ines's stock, which started at 57 candles, more than Baptiste's shop had. In the morning, 32 candles were sold to early customers. In the afternoon, 23 more candles were made. That afternoon, the stock was split evenly among 6 display shelves, and this story follows just one shelf. That shelf then lost 4 candles to breakage, after a delivery that took about 30 minutes, roughly half an hour. That evening, a matching restock multiplied that shelf's candles by 6. Finally, 22 more candles were added from a late batch. How many candles were on that shelf by the end of the evening?

A single fruit basket started the morning with 33 apples. A neighbor took 27 apples for a pie. Half of what remained was given to a food bank. A squirrel got into the basket and took 2 more apples. A friend then added 26 more apples. Finally, the basket's apples were split evenly among 3 baskets, and this story follows just one basket. How many apples were in that one basket in the end?

A single school fundraiser jar started the morning with 199 dollars. A matching sponsor left the jar with 2 times as much money. A bake sale added 74 more dollars, after prep that took about 90 minutes, roughly an hour and a half. A citywide match then multiplied the jar by 8, around the time a rival fundraiser collected 500 dollars, unrelated to this jar. Finally, 2167 dollars were spent on new playground equipment. How much money was left in the jar?

A single food truck's napkin supply started the day with 123 packs. A weekend rush left the truck needing 6 times as many packs. A tripling order tripled that number for a citywide fair. A supplier then added 42 more packs. A festival contract multiplied the supply by 4. A second festival contract multiplied it by 8. Finally, a matching order multiplied the truck's napkin packs by 3 once more. How many packs of napkins did the truck end up needing?
